chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn Isma'il from Salih ibn Uqba from Zayd al-Shahham, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'What is the reward for one who visits one of you?' He said, 'Like the reward of one who visited the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family).'

key_terms.أَهْلُ الْبَيْت: The People of the House (Ahl al-Bayt)
key_terms.صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ: Peace be upon him and his family

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for visiting the Imams according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the equivalence in spiritual reward between visiting the Imams and visiting the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH), underscoring their unique ontological status as the true heirs of prophethood. This comparison reflects the Shia theological principle that the Imams are the continuation of the Prophet’s light and authority, making their visitation a means of attaining proximity to the Divine through the Prophet’s lineage. The narration serves as a foundational text for the ritual importance of ziyarah in Shia piety, linking the believer’s devotion to the Ahl al-Bayt directly with the Prophet’s own status.
